deficiencies.description: The rewrite introduces a causal link ('because') asserting that benign tumours are common because it takes a great deal for them to become malignant, whereas the source text presents these as separate observations without a causal relationship.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: So benign tumors are actually incredibly common. Right? So it actually takes a lot for a benign tumor to become malignant in terms of, as I said, the number of changes that have to happen within a tumor.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: Benign tumours are extremely common, because it takes a great deal for a benign tumour to become malignant, given the number of changes that have to happen within a tumour.
deficiencies.studentHarm: A student would wrongly learn that benign tumours are common as a consequence of the high number of changes required for malignancy.

considerations.sourcePassage: So I've just put these numbers up just so that you can have a sense.
considerations.reason: The rewrite specifies 'a sense of incidence', which is faithful to the stated topic of the section ('talking about incidence').

considerations.sourcePassage: And then this is, if you like, the percentage of tumors that result in deaths.
considerations.reason: The rewrite phrase 'A further slide shows the percentage of tumours that result in deaths' accurately captures the lecturer's direct statement introducing the figure.

considerations.sourcePassage: But they are very difficult to treat. And so they progress very quickly, and they're lethal.
considerations.reason: 'And so' was used conversationally as a discourse filler rather than expressing a strict cause-and-effect relationship, so rendering these as co-occurring properties is acceptable.
